title: Building Agent Interfaces: Lessons from Chrome DevTools (MCP) for Agents — Michael Hablich, Google
talk_summary: A Google PM describes how Chrome DevTools was rebuilt as an agent-facing interface (MCP + CLI), learning that dumping raw multi-MB trace data into context fails and that agent-facing tools need semantic summaries, tight tool surfaces, self-healing errors, and measured fuel efficiency. The core transferable ideas are tokens-per-successful-outcome measurement, tool/description curation, and error messages designed for agent self-recovery.

takeaways.what_they_do: They measure interface efficiency as tokens (and tool calls, duration) divided by successful task completions, per user journey rather than globally, and use the per-journey bars to prioritize what to optimize next.
takeaways.evidence_quote: what tokens per successful outcome tell you is the fuel efficiency of your interface
takeaways.numbers: no hard numbers cited; per-use-case bar chart used to rank improvement targets

takeaways.technique: Semantic summaries instead of raw dumps
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of returning the full multi-MB trace JSON, the tool returns markdown semantic summaries pointing the agent at the relevant signal.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we didn't force the agent to read the entire book, the trace, but instead we just pointed it at the right sentence
takeaways.numbers: trace file described as multiple megabytes / ~50,000 lines of JSON that blew the context window

takeaways.what_they_do: Niche tools are hidden behind flags so they don't sit in default context; a 'slim mode' exposes only ~3 tools, trading extra agent turns for a much smaller context.
takeaways.numbers: slim mode exposes ~3 tools vs 25 in full mode

takeaways.what_they_do: They expose a CLI alongside MCP so agents can chain commands (grep the accessibility tree, pipe an ID into click), doing token-heavy post-processing locally instead of in the model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the token post-processing is happening on your computer

takeaways.what_they_do: They iterated tool error messages to include the fix hint (e.g. 'no history entry to navigate back to'), which let agents recover without human intervention; plus proactive detours and troubleshooting skills.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We actually added the last sentence, and that enabled the agent to self-heal

takeaways.technique: Description audit for intent and activation criteria
takeaways.what_they_do: They treat tool schemas as the agent's UI: state core function plus when to use it (activation criteria), citing that most MCP descriptions have quality smells; they warn over-long descriptions bias small models.
takeaways.numbers: 97% of MCP tool descriptions have quality smells (cited paper)
